title: A timed-out wait on a UI-thread job must cancel the job and make a late job clean up its files
rule: When a worker thread hands a job to the UI thread (main dispatch queue, GTK idle source, an event loop) and waits with a timeout, the timeout must reach the job: share a cancelled flag the caller sets when it gives up, have the job check it before it starts any write, and have a job that finishes after the caller left remove what it wrote (detect it by the flag or by a failed send on the reply channel). The caller's own cleanup guard runs before the late job writes, so it cannot cover that file. Test it with a stand-in job that writes after the timeout and assert no file is left.
rationale: E21.2 (#144): on macOS and Linux a PDF print that outlived the caller's 120 s wait still wrote its hidden .partial file next to the user's chosen path after fm-core had already removed it, leaving the file for good.
